title: Last used grouped window is not highlighted when textual list is activated
line: The textual list of a grouped task now highlights the window you used last, not always the top one.
explanation: GroupDialog.findActiveTaskIndex() only highlighted the group's child that matched tasksModel.activeTask. When another app (Dolphin) was active nothing matched, so the list kept its default current index 0 and highlighted the top window. The function now picks the child with the latest LastActivated timestamp from the tasks model (the active window always has the latest one), and positions the view on it once.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: Highlight the last used window in the textual list

The textual list for grouped tasks only looked for the active window, so
it highlighted its top entry whenever another app was active. Highlight
the window activated most recently instead, the active one if any.

BUG: 486309

media.caption: Master: picked "etc" from the Konsole list, focused Dolphin, reopened the list: the top entry "usr" is highlighted.
With the fix, same steps: "etc", the Konsole window used last, is highlighted.

review.text: Using AbstractTasksModel.LastActivated in GroupDialog.findActiveTaskIndex() is the right approach to highlight the most recently used grouped window when another app is active. However, comparing a JS Date against 0 breaks in positive UTC timezones during early-morning hours because libtaskmanager provides LastActivated as a QTime, and dropping the explicit tasksModel.activeTask check loses a safe fast-path for midnight wraparound or freshly restarted plasmashell.
changes: Do not initialize lastActivated to 0 or compare a JS Date against 0: libtaskmanager's LastActivated role is a QTime, which QML converts to a local-time Date on 1970-01-01 whose numeric value is negative between 00:00 and the local UTC offset (and 0 at 00:00 UTC), causing `activated > 0` to be false. Initialize `let lastActivated = null;` and check `if (activated && !isNaN(activated) && (lastActivated === null || activated > lastActivated))`.

Preserve the explicit `childIndex === tasksModel.activeTask` match (taking precedence before/within the loop) so an active window in the group is still highlighted even if its LastActivated is missing right after a plasmashell restart or wrapped across midnight.
